107.0.s.en: (1) The redeemed give thanks to God

107.0.0.en: O give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

107.0.1.en: 1- Giving thanks to God means two things: the confession of sins and thanksgiving for kindness. And they go together in prayer, and they confirm that He is good, and that His goodness is constant throughout life and for ever. And there is much evidence of this from the history of the people of God, for it is He who freed them from the slavery of Egypt, and it is He also who saved them from their enemies in the age of the Judges, and after this brought them back from the captivity in which they were scattered to Jerusalem. All this confirms the continuing care of God for His children however much they sin, as long as they repent and return to Him.

107.0.2.en: 2- The giving of thanks to God is fulfilled in the Church of the New Testament when we confess our sins, and thank Christ the Redeemer who freed us by His cross, and gave us the new life that extends to eternity. So this verse is a prophecy about the Church of the New Testament and the Kingdom of Heaven.

107.1.0.en: 2- Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy; 3- And gathered them out of the lands, from the east, and from the west, from the north, and from the sea.

107.1.1.en: Those whom God redeemed from the hand of their enemies share in giving thanks to God, that is, His people who were in the slavery of Egypt, and He brought them out of it by the ten plagues, and they crossed the Red Sea. As for Pharaoh, from whose hand He redeemed them, he was drowned with his army in the sea. And He redeemed them also from the hand of their enemies in the age of the Judges, and killed their enemies. And from the Babylonian captivity He redeemed them and brought them back to their country, while their enemies the Babylonians He destroyed at the hands of Media and Persia. For God gathered His people whom the Babylonians had scattered throughout the world, He gathered them from the east and the west; that is, from every place, and brought them back to live in peace and worship Him in Jerusalem.

107.1.2.en: I wish, my brother, that every day you would take care to give thanks to God, that is, to confess your sins and thank Him for His care of you throughout the day. So you humble yourself before Him because you offend Him by your sins, while He puts you to shame by His mercy and kindnesses. His love is wonderful, surpassing the mind.

107.2.s.en: (2) God's care for those wandering in the wilderness

107.2.0.en: 4- They wandered in the wilderness in a solitary way; they found no city to dwell in.

107.2.1.en: 1- The Psalm tells us of the wandering of the people of God in the wilderness of Sinai for forty years. There was no food or drink in the wilderness, but God permitted this because of their murmuring against Him and their refusal to enter the promised land, so He commanded that they should not enter this land but die in the wilderness. But at the same time in His fatherhood He was guiding them and leading them by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, and gave them manna and quails as food, and gave them water to drink from the rock, and kept them in the wilderness from all their enemies. So this shows the sins of mankind, and the mercy of God that keeps man and leads him to repentance, and teaches the sons who would enter the land of Canaan how to obey God, so that they might enjoy His overflowing love.

107.2.2.en: 2- This wandering in Sinai is a symbol of the wandering of mankind away from God before Christ and the inability of philosophy to satisfy it or bring it to God; until Christ became incarnate in the fullness of time.

107.3.0.en: 6- Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses. 7- And he led them forth by the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation.

107.3.1.en: 1- When the people of God wandered in the wilderness of Sinai they felt their sin, and repented, and cried out to God during the forty years, so He forgave them and guided them to return to Him and keep His commandments. Then He brought their sons into cities to dwell in them in the land of Canaan, which flows with milk and honey. So crying out and prayer to God is always the only solution that draws out the mercies of the tender God, and so He shows His love and care for His children.

107.3.2.en: 2- In the Old Testament the prophets cried out for the nations that were wandering far from God; until in the fullness of time He guided them to the right way, which is faith in Christ, who declared that He is the way, the truth and the life (Jn 14:6).

107.3.3.en: 3- Verse six is repeated four times in this Psalm to confirm the necessity of crying out to God at all times, and especially in afflictions, for then God's tenderness and His love, which surpasses every mind, appear, and His forgiveness of all sins.

107.4.0.en: 8- Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! 9- For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.

107.4.1.en: 1- In the face of the greatness of God's love the Psalm calls to the confession of God's love, and thanks to Him for it. For this is the meaning of giving thanks. God's wonders and miracles are many, and His miracle appears here in satisfying two million souls with food and drink in a dry wilderness in which life is very difficult.

107.4.2.en: 2- (Verse 8) is repeated four times in this Psalm to confirm the importance of giving thanks to God, which binds the soul to His love, and protects it and keeps it from sin and makes its life happy, so it delights in fellowship with God.

107.4.3.en: If affliction is something you do not like, trust that it is by God's arrangement to awaken your soul, so you pray fervently and seek God's help. Cry out to Him, and you will receive His mercies and return to hear His voice and rejoice in fellowship with Him.

107.5.0.en: 10- Such as sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, being bound in affliction and iron; 11- Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High: 12- Therefore he brought down their heart with labour; they fell down, and there was none to help.

107.5.1.en: Contemned the counsel of the most High: rejected the word of God.

107.5.3.en: 1- The Psalm here speaks of those imprisoned in slavery when the people of God were in Egypt, and the Egyptians humbled them and forced them to labor. And this humiliation was repeated in the age of the Judges when they were negligent toward their enemies and mingled with them, so they rose against them and humbled them.

107.5.4.en: 2- This prison and these fetters mean falling into sins and desires. And this happened to the people of God when they mingled with the pagans and worshipped idols. And it happens today when a person is negligent and falls into sin, and Satan humbles him, especially in the sin of pride, so God forsakes him, and Satan humbles him and God does not help him; because he does not repent and return to God because of his pride, which delays repentance.

107.5.5.en: 3- These verses tell us of the humiliation of mankind condemned to death in the Old Testament. And all, even the righteous, used to go to Hades; until Christ accomplished redemption on the cross, and brought up those who believe in Him to Paradise.

107.6.0.en: 13- Then they cry unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saveth them out of their distresses. 14- He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder. 15- Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! 16- For he hath broken the gates of brass, and cut the bars of iron in sunder.

107.6.1.en: The verses are repeated here (vv. 13, 15) as the people of God cry out to Him, and He frees them from their slavery however strong it is, like iron and brass; because some sins are difficult, such as pride, the return of sin, and despair. But the power of God works miracles and wonders, so He frees His children and brings them back to enjoy life with Him.

107.6.2.en: Do not be troubled by the multitude of your sins, or their ugliness; because your God is strong and able to free you from them. And however much your circumstances bind you to sin, He is able to change the circumstances, or to support you, so you rise above evil and are delivered from it. Only take refuge in Him with humble and persevering prayer, and you will receive your freedom and regain your joy.

107.7.0.en: 17- Fools because of their transgression, and because of their iniquities, are afflicted. 18- Their soul abhorreth all manner of meat; and they draw near unto the gates of death.

107.7.1.en: 1- The fools are those who go far from God, so they fall into many sins that humble them, and put them in distress and despair; until they lose their appetite for food and drink. And diseases may strike them as a result of their thoughts and their agitation, which contribute to the loss of appetite for food, which increases their weakness, so they become perplexed and anxious.

107.7.2.en: 2- These fools fall into sins that increase their distance from God; until they lose their spiritual appetite, that is, they lose their longing for prayer, for reading the word of God, and for being in the house of the Lord.

107.7.3.en: Although the spiritual food is before them, they do not benefit from it; until they almost die spiritually, that is, they fall not only into coldness but into spiritual dryness.

107.8.0.en: 19- Then they cry unto the Lord in their trouble, and he saveth them out of their distresses. 20- He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions. 21- Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!

107.8.1.en: 22- And let them sacrifice the sacrifices of thanksgiving, and declare his works with rejoicing.

107.8.2.en: Declare his works: recount His works one by one.

107.8.3.en: 1- Here, as we mentioned, the two verses (vv. 19, 20) are repeated, which show the people of God taking refuge in Him, then God's answering them with great miracles. And we see the tenderness of God who heals His children of the disease of sin, and also of bodily diseases if need be, that is, He forgives them and gives them spiritual health and vitality, so they come to Him and worship Him with joy, and offer Him the sacrifices of thanksgiving, that is, the praise of the lips, and thank Him for His works with them.

107.8.4.en: 2- The word of God that God sends is a prophecy about the Incarnation of Christ, who heals the diseases of mankind that believes in Him, and transfers it from death to life, so it praises Him and thanks Him for ever, and they enjoy the sacrifice of thanksgiving, which is the sacrament of Holy Communion of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

107.8.5.en: How great are Your works with me, O Lord, which are manifested in Your receiving me while I am fallen in sin and unable to rise from it, so You stretch out Your hand, and accept my repentance and turn me from death to life, so I rise and praise You, and enjoy being with You.

107.9.s.en: (5) God's care for those traveling on the sea

107.9.0.en: 23- They that go down to the sea in ships, that do business in great waters; 24- These see the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep. 25- For he commandeth, and raiseth the stormy wind, which lifteth up the waves thereof. 26- They mount up to the heaven, they go down again to the depths: their soul is melted because of trouble. 27- They reel to and fro, and stagger like a drunken man, and all their wisdom is swallowed up.

107.9.1.en: 1- The Psalm speaks of the merchants traveling on the sea, and the sailors, and the suffering they meet in traveling through the sea. And it shows that God is the mover of nature and the Upholder of all, for it is He who commands, and the winds are stirred up, and the waves rise. So the ships are lifted up toward heaven. Then they go down toward the depth, and the passengers of the ship reel violently like a drunken man, and face death, and their hearts melt with fear, and they lose their ability to control the ship, and surrender to the hand of God, as happened with Jonah and the passengers of the ship when they were traveling on the sea (Jon 1:4).

107.9.2.en: 2- The merchants and sailors are a symbol of the spiritual person who crosses the sea of this world, and God permits him afflictions, which are the winds and waves, and he faces joys and sufferings, which are the rising to heaven and the going down to the depth, and his soul is pressed, and he faces death, or is exposed to severe psychological pressure, and finds nothing before him but to surrender into the hand of God.

107.9.3.en: 3- The merchants and sailors are also a symbol of the prophets, Apostles, priests and servants in every generation who proclaim God, so they face many afflictions and troubles, and during them they experience God, who lifts them to heaven. And they also face psychological troubles by their going down to the depth, and they have nothing before the afflictions but to commit their souls into the hand of God.

107.10.0.en: 28- Then they cry unto the Lord in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distresses. 29- He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. 30- Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven. The haven that

107.10.1.en: they desire. 31- Oh that men would praise the Lord for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! 32- Let them exalt him also in the congregation of the people, and praise him in the assembly of the elders.

107.10.3.en: 1- Those who suffer in their travel within the sea have nothing before them but to cry out to God to rescue them, so He intervenes in His fatherhood and calms the storm, and they regain their peace, and even thank God, and tell of His wonders everywhere among the peoples, and in the gathering of the rulers and the great.

107.10.4.en: 2- The spiritual people and the servants cry out to God in their afflictions, so He intervenes and rescues them from them and their souls grow calm, and they feel the power of God who protects them, so they praise Him for His wonderful works with them, whether in the gathering of peoples and nations, so they guide them to faith, or in the gatherings of the servants and the spiritual teachers, so their faith is confirmed, and they glorify God.

107.10.5.en: Afflictions are permitted by God not to trouble you, but to awaken your soul, so you move in fervent prayers, and experience the work of God and rejoice, and your zeal for praise and thanksgiving increases all the days of your life.

107.11.0.en: 33- He turneth rivers into a wilderness, and the watercourses into thirsty ground; 34- A fruitful land into barrenness, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein.

107.11.1.en: Wilderness: dry deserted land without water or life.

107.11.2.en: Thirsty ground: land in which there is no water, but in which every man, animal and plant is thirsty.

107.11.3.en: Barrenness: ruined, unfit for farming or dwelling.

107.11.4.en: The Psalm shows the seriousness of the evil that people walk in, for it angers God, so He permits them distress in the hope that they will repent, so He makes places with much water, such as rivers and watercourses, completely dry, and the fertile land ruined, to the degree that it is fit for nothing. So when the wicked see their material distress they return to God whom they angered and neglected.

107.12.0.en: 35- He turneth the wilderness into a standing water, and dry ground into watersprings. 36- And there he maketh the hungry to dwell, that they may prepare a city for habitation; 37- And sow the fields, and plant vineyards, which may yield fruits of increase. 38- He blesseth them also, so that they are multiplied greatly; and suffereth not their cattle to decrease.

107.12.1.en: Standing water: a small river whose waters run quietly.

107.12.2.en: 1- These verses show God's work with the humble believers, for He blesses them and gives them the water that gives life to them, and to their animals so they multiply, and to their land so they sow it, and reap many fruits and crops.

107.12.3.en: 2- To the poor in spirit who repent with humility God gives many spiritual blessings, so the Holy Spirit works in them, who is symbolized by the waters, and bestows on them the fruits of the Holy Spirit, which are symbolized by the fruits of the earth, the produce and the cattle, so they rejoice and thank God.

107.13.0.en: 39- Again, they are minished and brought low through oppression, affliction, and sorrow. 40- He poureth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to wander in the wilderness, where there is no way. A wandering place: a place in which a person wanders because there are no roads, like the deserts.

107.13.1.en: 1- If God blesses people, then they return to being immersed in their sins, He removes His grace from them, and their good things decrease, water, fruits and cattle, so they grow weak and many of them die, so they are fewer in number, because of their evils, and their souls that are troubled by the scarcity of their material resources, and He even permits the humiliation, disgrace and straying of their guides and rulers who lead them. So they all go astray because they follow their rulers, that is, God forsakes them so they face many afflictions; that they may take heed and repent.

107.13.2.en: 2- Afflictions meet the spiritual people; so that they hold fast to God. And God permits the humiliation of their rulers, that is, their minds that go astray, and their feelings that err, so they humiliate their bodies. And when they see their calamity they return to God with repentance. As happened with David the prophet.

107.14.0.en: 41- Yet setteth he the poor on high from affliction, and maketh him families like a flock. The poor is the humble one, who takes refuge in God in repentance; for if the righteous have faced afflictions because of their falling into evil, yet when they repent He lifts them up and blesses them, so their tribes multiply like flocks of sheep in their abundance. And God shepherds them all in His love, so they are in unity. And this shows the extent of God's long-suffering and mercy, who is long-suffering toward His children, so He blesses them if they keep His commandments, and permits them afflictions if they go far from Him, but if they repent He returns and lifts them up, and blesses them a second time, as happened with Job, who was a righteous man whom God blessed, then permitted him afflictions, to be freed from self-righteousness, and when he repented He blessed him again greatly, that is, He gave him double what he had had.

107.15.0.en: 42- The righteous shall see it, and rejoice: and all iniquity shall stop her mouth. 43- Whoso is wise, and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord.

107.15.1.en: The Psalm ends with these golden words, calling the believers and the upright in their lives to understand God's care for His children from the beginning of the Psalm to its end. And especially in this last part; that they may keep away from evil and hold fast to God, and that every wicked person may fall silent after the Psalm has exposed the end of evil (vv. 33, 34, 39, 40). And it calls the upright to keep these words not only in their hearts but in their conduct. And to understand, and always meditate on God's mercies and His care for mankind; that they may thank Him and praise Him.

107.15.2.en: Be watchful so that you live with God with exactness, and hasten to repentance if you sin, so you always enjoy God's care, and His mercies overflow upon you, and the blessings of the Holy Spirit work in you, and you taste the sweetness of fellowship with God.

107.15.3.en: The praise of God the Victor is His praise. A Psalm of David: "O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory" (v. 1) Introduction:

107.15.4.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, as the Psalm mentions.

107.15.6.en: When David was fighting Aram, Edom took this opportunity, united with Moab, and they attacked the south of the land of the children of Israel, so David sent Joab the commander of his army, and he fought Edom and defeated it.

107.15.7.en: 3- This Psalm is made up of two parts borrowed from the previous Psalms. And these two parts are:

107.15.8.en: a- The verses (vv. 1-5) are those found in (Ps 57:7-11).

107.15.9.en: b- The verses (vv. 6-13) are those found in (Ps 60:5-12).

107.15.10.en: 4- This Psalm is full of hope and suits every person who needs hope, whether he is passing through an affliction, or has come out of it, so it confirms his hope.

107.15.11.en: 5- This Psalm was repeated in the communal worship of the Jews, especially after victory in wars, for it is a liturgical Psalm, that is, the congregation prays it together in worship.

107.15.12.en: 6- Those who compiled the Psalms took this Psalm from the two mentioned Psalms (Pss 57, 60), which David wrote; so that they would be a Psalm of praise and thanksgiving to God and give a feeling of victory over the enemies.

107.15.13.en: 7- There are no differences between this Psalm and the Psalms taken from, except in very few words that do not affect the meaning, and they are:

107.15.14.en: a- Verse (1) "even with my glory" and in (Ps 57:8) "awake up, my glory".

107.15.15.en: b- Verse (2) "Awake, psaltery and harp" and in (Ps 57:18) "Awake, O psaltery, and O harp".

107.15.16.en: c- Verse (4) "great above the heavens" and in (Ps 57:10) "great unto the heavens".

107.15.17.en: 8- The title of this Psalm shows the importance of man's praising God with his whole being, for the title says "his praise".

107.15.18.en: A Psalm of David. Praise belongs to the mind, and the tongue expresses it. And "Psalm" means what is accompanied by a musical instrument, which is the pipe, and the mouth and the hands share in it.

107.15.19.en: 9- The first part of this Psalm (vv. 1-5) is found in Psalm number 56 in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Sixth Hour, as we praise God crucified for us; that He may save us from our sins.

107.15.21.en: 1- O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory. 2- Awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early. 3- I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. 4- For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. 5- Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth.

107.15.22.en: See the interpretation of Psalm 57 in the Encyclopedia, Volume Eleven. In general this part tells us of the steadfastness of the spiritual person in praising and glorifying God; so that he wakes early, with his musical instruments, to praise God for His many mercies.

107.15.23.en: (2) God the helper of His people (vv. 6-13):

107.15.24.en: 6- That thy beloved may be delivered: save with thy right hand, and answer me. 7- God hath spoken in his holiness: I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth. 8- Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the helmet of my head; Judah is my sceptre.

107.15.25.en: 9- Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; O Philistia, shout aloud over me. 10- Who will lead me into the fortified city? who will bring me into Edom? 11- Is it not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and thou goest not forth, O God, with our armies?

107.15.26.en: 12- Give us help in trouble: for vain is the salvation of man. 13- Through God we shall do valiantly, and he shall tread down our enemies.

107.15.27.en: See the interpretation of this part in Psalm sixty, which is in the Encyclopedia, Volume Eleven.

107.15.28.en: And it is to be noted that this part speaks to us of the intervention of the mighty God to rescue His people, and give them victory over their enemies, and it returns the power to God, and not to weak man.

107.15.29.en: God rescues the righteous and punishes the wicked. To the chief Musician. For David. A Psalm: "Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise" (v. 1) Introduction:

107.15.30.en: 1- Its writer: David the prophet, as the title of the Psalm mentions.

107.15.31.en: 2- When was it written? After David reigned over all the tribes of the children of Israel, and took Ahithophel as a counselor and a friend to him.

107.15.32.en: 3- This Psalm expresses David's sufferings from the betrayal of those close to him, and asks for deliverance from God to save him from their hands. So it is the cry of one who suffers and at the same time with the eye of prophecy he saw God's punishment of them. This reassured him, and confirmed his faith in the just God, who keeps him and protects him.

107.15.33.en: 4- This Psalm suits everyone who is exposed to offenses or betrayal from those close to him, for it gives him hope in God who is able to protect him and compensate him for what he lost.

107.15.34.en: 5- This Psalm is Messianic because it prophesies about Christ, who was exposed to many sufferings for our salvation, and speaks clearly of the betrayal of Judas Iscariot, and the punishment that will come upon him.

107.15.35.en: 6- In the title of this Psalm in the Septuagint it says "to the end", and by it he means the wicked's completing their evil, and Christ's completing the salvation by His death on the cross, as David, who is a type of Christ, completed his endurance of the wicked, and their betrayal, and God's rescue of him.

107.15.36.en: 7- The Book of Acts quoted from this Psalm, and confirms that its writer is David, and this Psalm was fulfilled in the betrayal of Judas Iscariot (Acts 1:15-20).

107.15.37.en: 8- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
